newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures ends lower, seen technically weak.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures ends lower, seen technically weak.

text.p: Frozen concentrated orange juice futures climbed higher early, filled a gap on the charts and then sank back below unchanged by the close.

Early local and speculative buying buoyed May to a high of 79.50 after filling the gap between 78.00 and 79.20. Steady trade selling coupled with light local and speculative selling pressured May to a low of 76.90.
The spot month ended down 0.30 cent at 77.05, while the deferred contracts settled 0.25 lower to 0.65 higher.
Volume was estimated at 5,000 lots compared to Wednesday's official 2,989 lots.

Analysts said the market was due for a correction after five consecutive days of lower prices. The failure of the May contract to rally to the nine-day moving average of 79.90 and fill a second gap on the charts from 83.15 to 82.95 made on March 26 shows that further losses may be in store, however.
Support in May was pegged at the contract low of 75.50.

Market sources said a strike at Brazil's key port of Santos may have brought in early speculative buying although orange juice was still loading at the dock. Much of the loading of juice has been automated and does not depend on dockworkers.
Players await May options expiry on Friday, and the weekly movement figure released later today. The market expects the movement to fall below 5 million gallons due to the short holiday week.
